reviewItem.question: If an exposed environment does nothing about "Line added to cmd/crossplane/core/core.go: return errors.New(\"the --registry flag is no longer supported since support for a default registry value has been…", what happens, and is that review or action? proposed: workload-failure

consequence.statement: If the Crossplane core pod is still started with --registry, the core command returns the error "the --registry flag is no longer supported since support for a default registry value has been removed" and does not run.
consequence.remediation: Remove --registry from the Crossplane args and make sure every package, and each of its dependencies, uses a fully qualified name that states its registry.

proposed.statement: In v2.0.0 the Crossplane core command no longer supports the --registry flag: setting it returns the error "the --registry flag is no longer supported since support for a default registry value has been removed", and all packages and their dependencies must use fully qualified names that state their registry.
